questions.question:

questions.question:
Which two signs should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct?

5 × 15 ÷ 7 - 20 + 4 = 77
questions.solution:
Given equation: 5 × 15 ÷ 7 - 20 + 4 = 77

Interchanging signs: (÷ and +)

5 × 15 + 7 – 20 ÷ 4

According to BODMAS rule.

5 × 15 + 7 – 20 ÷ 4

= 5 × 15 + 7 – 5

= 82 - 5

= **77**

Hence, after interchanging (÷ and +) the equation becomes correct.

questions.question: A train covers 60 km at a uniform speed. If the speed had been 8 km/h more, it would have taken 10 hours less for the same journey. What is the speed of the train (in km/h)?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let the speed of train be x km /h

Distance = 60 km

So, time = 60 / x

When speed is 8 km/h more, time taken = 60/(x + 8)

According to the question,

⇒ 60/x - 60/(x + 8) = 10

⇒ 60 × (x + 8 - x)/x(x + 8) = 10

⇒ 60 × 8 = x(x + 8)

⇒ 48 = x² + 8x 

⇒ x² + 8x – 48 = 0

⇒ x² + 12x - 4x - 48 = 0 

⇒ x(x + 12) - 4(x + 12) = 0

⇒ (x + 12)(x – 4) = 0

⇒ x = 4 or – 12

But x being speed cannot be negative.

So, x = 4

**∴ The speed of the train is 4 km/h.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

Concept use:

Distance = (S1 × S2)/(S1 - S2) × (time difference)

Where S1 & S2 are the speed before and after respectively.

Calculation:

Let's assume that the initial speed of the train is x km/hr

After the speed becomes (x + 8), so,

⇒ ((x+8) times x)/(8) × 10 = 60

⇒ (x + 8) × x = 48

Now, from the option test, the option A (4) satisfies the equation

⇒ x = 4

∴ The speed of the train is 4 km/hr
